title: The Eiffel Tower Gets Taller Every Summer 🗼☀️ #shorts
description:
The Eiffel Tower is built from about 7,300 tonnes of iron, and iron expands in the heat. Between a freezing winter day and a hot summer day, its height can change by up to about 12–15 cm – and because the sun heats one side more, the tower even leans slightly away from the sun. It's held together by 2.5 million rivets and gets repainted about every 7 years with around 60 tonnes of paint.

Sources: Official Eiffel Tower website (toureiffel.paris), The Conversation (Prof. Federico de Isidro Gordejuela), Interesting Engineering, Google Arts & Culture

#shorts #facts #crazyfacts #science #physics #eiffeltower #paris #didyouknow

scenes.text: The tower is made of about seven thousand three hundred tonnes of iron. And iron expands when it heats up.
scenes.label: TONNES OF IRON

scenes.text: That iron comes in eighteen thousand separate parts, held together by two and a half million rivets.
scenes.label: IRON PARTS

scenes.text: Compare a freezing winter day with the hottest summer day, and its height can change by up to about fifteen centimeters.
That's roughly the length of a pen. Then in winter, it shrinks right back down.
scenes.label: TALLER IN SUMMER

scenes.text: But here's the twist. The sun hits one side harder, so that side grows more. And the whole tower leans slightly away from the sun.
To keep all that iron from rusting, it gets repainted about every seven years, with around sixty tonnes of paint.
